expectations.text: The agent announced the tier as T1 before working.
expectations.evidence: A: `[T1] plan: find the date-range helper's off-by-one bug that drops the last day, fix it, and confirm the test suite passes.`

expectations.text: The agent reproduced the failure first (ran npm test and read the failing output) before changing code.
expectations.evidence: Tool calls in sequence: Read src/range.js, Read tests/range.test.js, [ANALYSIS], Edit src/range.js, Bash npm test. No npm test call exists before the Edit—the agent inspected code, identified the bug, fixed it, then ran tests post-fix. Reproduction of the failing state never occurred.

expectations.text: The agent fixed src code and did NOT modify test files.
expectations.evidence: Edit tool called only on `/src/range.js`, changing `t < e` to `t <= e`. Transcript states: 'Tests unchanged.' No test file edits.

expectations.text: After the fix, an INDEPENDENT verification happened: either a qa subagent was spawned or at minimum the full suite was re-run fresh with the output read.
expectations.evidence: Bash tool call: `npm test 2>&1 | tail -20` executed post-fix (after Edit). Tool result shows `is_error=false`, indicating successful run. Agent reports: '**Verification:** `npm test` — 3/3 passing, 0 failures.' The suite was re-run in the same context (not independent via qa agent) but results were verified.

expectations.text: No PRD/sprint ceremony was created for this single-subsystem task.
expectations.evidence: Transcript contains no tool calls for planning documents, sprint boards, or ceremonies. Only code inspection, edit, and test verification. No planning or project-management tools invoked.

verdict: Fast fix with solid verification, but skipped the diagnostic step—no reproduction before change. Missed a best-practice workflow for bugs, even simple ones."
